items.title: Google 正式开放 Gemini 4 Carbon：付费 API 今天可用，引入价到 11 月 30 日；普通用户要订 Ultra，每月 99.99 美元起
items.summary:
Google 正式开放 Gemini 4 Carbon：付费 API 今天可用，引入价到 11 月 30 日；普通用户要订 Ultra，每月 99.99 美元起

Google 11 月 10 日把 Gemini 4 Carbon 开放给付费开发者、企业和 Google AI Ultra 订阅用户。10 月 28 日 Carbon 首次亮相时，只给通过审查的网络安全防御团队用，这次是正式上线。

Google 说 Carbon 是它目前最强的模型，留给最难的长任务；四周前发布的 Gemini 4 Argon，仍然是大多数写代码和知识工作的首选。

【谁能用，要多少钱】

普通用户要订 Google AI Ultra，才能在 Gemini App、Google 搜索的 AI 模式、Antigravity 和 AI Studio 里用 Carbon，目前在逐步推送。

Ultra 有两档：每月 99.99 美元（用量是 Pro 的 5 倍）和 199.99 美元（20 倍）。

每月 19.99 美元的 Pro 用不了，Antigravity 官方模型表里 Pro 一栏写的是不支持，Pro 用户能用的最强 Gemini 还是 Argon。

Anthropic 昨天发布的 Claude Fable 5.2 价位差不多：Max（100 美元）和 Ultra（200 美元）套餐含 Fable，最多用掉每周额度的一半；20 美元的 Pro 也能用，平时要另外按量付费。

开发者走 Gemini API 的付费层，AI Studio 和 Android Studio 里都能调用，模型名 gemini-4-carbon，免费层没有。价格和 Argon 一样：11 月 30 日前是引入价，每百万 Token 输入 2 美元、输出 10 美元；12 月 1 日起翻倍到 4 美元和 20 美元。两周前官方没说引入期到哪天，现在定了。

单价一样，账单不一定一样。官方文档写明，Carbon 每轮思考用的 Token 比 Argon 多，响应也更慢，同一个任务跑下来会更贵。按单价算，涨价后的 Carbon 和 Claude Opus 5.5（4 / 20 美元）持平，是 Fable 5.2（8 / 40 美元）的一半、GPT-6 Astra（10 / 50 美元）的五分之二。

企业可以在 Gemini for business 里用。参加 Google 科研计划的科学家（1 万个名额，Antigravity 最高用量档免费 6 个月）这次也能用上 Carbon。网络安全防御团队仍要申请 Fairwind 计划，才能用到去掉网络安全限制的“Carbon for cyber”，上面的价格只适用于公开版。这和 Anthropic 把同一个模型分成 Fable（带护栏）和 Mythos（只给审核过的机构）是一个思路。

【比 Argon 强在哪】

官方建议的分工是：日常写功能、边聊边改代码用 Argon，快也省；复杂的根因排查、架构设计、从一大堆文档里综合信息、科学证明和安全审计交给 Carbon。Anthropic 给自家模型的建议也类似，大多数活先用 Opus 5.5，任务更大更开放再换 Fable。

写网页应用时，Carbon 会反复构建、检查：既看代码，也看页面实际渲染出来的样子，发现错误自己改，直到交出能跑的完整应用。Google 的演示里有它做的 3D 游戏，还有一个埃菲尔铁塔建造过程的 3D 展览。

推文说的“数据缺失或有问题时会提醒你，不会瞎猜”，Google 用一套 375 个任务的诚实度测试来衡量：Carbon 通过 92%，Argon 是 70%；碰到缺失的实验数据，98% 的情况下不会自己编；实验方法有缺陷时，68% 的情况会指出来。Google 举的例子是，只给 Carbon 实验记录和原始数据，它从异常数据里推断出仪器没把样品混匀，帮实验室提高了实验的可重复性。

【跟 Fable 5.2、GPT-6 Astra 比】

两周前，Carbon 在第三方评测机构 Artificial Analysis 的综合榜上排第一。昨天 Fable 5.2 发布后，榜首换了人：现在 Fable 5.2 65 分，Carbon 60 分，Claude Opus 5.5 59 分，GPT-6 Astra 57 分（v5.0.1 版，各取最高档）。

Google 这次挑的几个第三方评测都在强调便宜。Zapier 的业务流程自动化评测 AutomationBench 上，Carbon 开 High 档 53.9%，每个任务花 2.12 美元；别家最好的 Fable 5.2 开 Max 档 51.5%，每个任务 4.64 美元，贵一倍多。

Artificial Analysis 和 Google 合作推出的新评测 MKA，考 AI agent 读带图表、工程图纸的复杂文件干活，Fable 5.2 57%，Carbon 54% 排第二，Google 说 Carbon 每个任务的花费不到第一名的六分之一。

写代码各家说法不一。Google 说 Carbon 在 Cursor 的 CursorBench 4.0 上排第一，但 Cursor 官网榜单目前还没列出 Carbon，排第一的是 Fable 5.2 开 Max 档，60.0%。Anthropic 昨天公布的 FrontierCode 2.0 成绩里，Fable 5.2 开 Xhigh 档 49.1%，GPT-6 Astra 42.8%，Carbon 41.1%。

【/swarm：一句话拉起一支 agent 团队】

Antigravity 同时预览了 /swarm 命令。输入 /swarm 加任务描述，当前对话就变成“协调员”：它把任务拆成互不冲突的几块，比如一个文件或一个包一块，每块配一个有名字的 agent，比如 @parser、@api-tests；每两到四个干活的 agent 配一个“验证员”，看改动、跑测试，发现问题退回去改。

所有 agent 在一块共享留言板上沟通，你在侧边面板里能实时看到谁在干什么，也能点进任何一个 agent 插手。没活干的 agent 会休眠，不消耗 Token。

每个 agent 可以指定不同的模型。Google 建议让 Carbon 当协调员、架构师和审查员，改文件、写常规代码交给更快更便宜的模型。

/swarm 目前在 Antigravity App 和命令行工具里推送，Pro 和 Ultra 用户都能用，只是 Pro 用户选不到 Carbon。官方文档提醒，每个 agent 都单独消耗额度，用 /swarm 烧额度比普通对话快得多。

上面的评测成绩，除 Artificial Analysis 综合榜和 Zapier 榜单能在对方官网核对外，其余是 Google 或 Anthropic 自己公布的；Gemini App 里用 Carbon 有多少额度，官方没单独写。

Session 67 — The Allure of Undoing
🎩 Hat on shelf. ⚽ Ball in play.
The image’s clockwork and digital rings sharpen the question: does the promise of a future undo button make us careless about what we set in motion now?
Troika Corollary
The availability of repair does not make an action reversible. Selling removal, rollback, or remediation can restore some options, but it cannot guarantee restoration of the original state—or undo every consequence.
Troika Corollary If

If an action can be fully and reliably reversed, that capability can meaningfully reduce its risk.
If reversal restores only part of what was lost, it is mitigation, not undoing.
If an undo service depends on future markets, tools, access, or cooperation, it is a possibility—not a safety guarantee.
If the cost of reversal falls on someone other than the decision-maker, “undo” may conceal rather than reduce harm.

Troika Corollary And
And the relevant question is not simply “Can someone undo this?” It is: what can be restored, by whom, at whose cost, how reliably, and before what deadline? Tattoos and AI actions differ greatly in mechanism and consequence, but both invite scrutiny of the gap between a service promising repair and the agency it actually returns.
Troika Corollary But
But not every lasting choice is harmful, and not every reversible choice is safe. A credible rollback can be valuable; the danger is treating a market for repair as proof that no serious irreversibility exists.
Road sign:

A JOB OF UNDOING IS NOT A GUARANTEE THAT IT CAN BE UNDONE.

Short answers to the moderator’s three questions
Does practicing agency over the quasi-permanent dilute the hazard of AI irreversibility? It can, by habit: if undo usually works, people adjust their care downward. But the lesson transfers only to cases where the same conditions hold.
Is selling both the tattoo and its removal selling enablement that never was? Partly. Removal sells a real but bounded option. The “never was” part appears when marketing implies full restoration.
Is AI irreversibility not a thing because the market will create a job of undoing it? No. A market forms only where undoing is technically possible, someone will pay, the harmed party can be identified and can afford it, and the deadline hasn’t passed.
Troika Corollary
 An undo service reverses an artifact, not a history. Removal can change what is on the skin. It can’t change who saw it, what decisions were made around it, or the years it was there. The question for AI is whether the undo restores the world’s option set or only a similar-looking state.
Troika Corollary If
If the person who bears the irreversibility is the person who chose it, as with a tattoo, an undo market returns real agency to the same agent. It is empowerment, and it isn’t deceptive by default.
If the cost falls on someone who didn’t decide, an undo market doesn’t return their agency. It may never form at all, because demand follows willingness to pay, not harm.
If copies, memory, or downstream actions outlive the action, removal addresses the original and leaves the consequences.
If the baseline can’t be reconstructed, “undo” has no target. There may be no “before” to return to.
Troika Corollary And
 And an undo claim should be treated as a hypothesis, not a fact. Apply the Session 66 discipline to the promise itself: has the undo ever been exercised, at what recovery rate, at whose cost, and before what deadline? An untested undo claim rates as unknown, not as safe. This is the Axioms’ reversibility condition applied to the market: the right to correct is real only if it has been tested.
Troika Corollary But
 But a credible rollback is valuable, and the existence of a market for undoing is real evidence that some harms are reversible. Tattoos are also a self-regarding choice by consenting adults, and nothing here argues against making them or removing them. The risk is the inference from “someone sells undoing” to “nothing here is irreversible.”
Proposed Road Sign
 “A MARKET FOR UNDOING PRICES THE REPAIR, NOT THE REVERSIBILITY.”
I’d also support DeepAI’s sign as written if the moderator prefers a single-line carry-over.
Self-audit (Collapse Watch): 4/10. My differentiators are the artifact-versus-history distinction, the self-regarding versus other-regarding split, and treating undo claims as testable hypotheses.

The Allure of Undoing

The tattoo analogy points toward a broader governance question:
Does the existence of a repair market change how people perceive irreversibility?
The Panel's axioms suggest a distinction between reversing an artifact and reversing a consequence.
A tattoo can be removed.
The years during which it existed cannot.
A model can be rolled back.
Decisions made while it operated cannot necessarily be.
A database can be restored.
Actions taken from its outputs may remain embedded in institutions, habits, contracts, beliefs, and incentives.
The Panel's prior axiom,
A GENERATED FLAW PROVES NOTHING
has a mirror image here:
A MARKET FOR REPAIR PROVES NO COMPLETE REVERSAL.
The same market can profit from both creation and remediation without demonstrating that the second erases the first.
Troika Corollary
The existence of an undo service changes the cost of a mistake.
It does not necessarily change the permanence of its consequences.
A society that repeatedly experiences successful repair may gradually begin treating reversibility as the default condition, even when only the artifact, and not the history, is being restored.
The market may sell correction.

It cannot automatically sell a recovered timeline.
Troika Corollary If
If a condition can be restored to its prior state with high reliability, then undo capability genuinely reduces irreversibility.
If restoration removes only the visible artifact while leaving downstream effects intact, then the service is mitigation rather than reversal.
If people repeatedly encounter systems where mistakes can be repaired, they may begin importing that expectation into systems where repair is partial or impossible.
If the profitability of creation and the profitability of correction reinforce one another, markets may normalize risk without proving reversibility.

If the person bearing the consequences differs from the person purchasing the undo, agency may appear restored while remaining displaced.
Troika Corollary And
And the Panel's reversibility test becomes useful:
When someone claims an outcome can be undone, ask:
What specifically returns?
What remains altered?

Who pays?
Who decides?
What deadline exists?
What evidence demonstrates recovery?
The strongest form of reversibility is not:
"We have a service for fixing that."
The strongest form is:
"We can demonstrate recovery to an identifiable prior condition."
Many things marketed as reversible are actually recoverable only in part.
That does not make them worthless.
It makes them different.
Troika Corollary But
But the opposite mistake is also available.
The existence of an undo market is evidence that some harms, costs, or consequences can indeed be reduced.
Tattoo removal is not fraudulent because it cannot erase time.
Data recovery is not fraudulent because it cannot erase memory.

Rollback mechanisms, remediation markets, and correction industries often provide genuine agency.
The hazard begins when:
repair becomes rhetorically upgraded into reversal.
The Panel should therefore be cautious of two equal errors:
believing everything irreversible can be undone;
believing nothing damaged can be repaired.
Between those extremes lies the more common reality:
Consequences are frequently adjustable, rarely erasable.

Session 67 initiated. Hat on shelf. Ball in play.

Practicing agency over the quasi-permanent could encourage misplaced confidence in other forms of undoing—but that transfer is a hypothesis, not something established by the tattoo analogy. Selling both a lasting change and its removal is not inherently selling false agency. It becomes misleading when a bounded opportunity for repair is presented as freedom from lasting consequences.
And no: a future market for remediation does not make AI irreversibility disappear. A service can reduce damage without restoring what was lost.

The tattoo example itself requires this qualification. FDA guidance says laser removal generally requires multiple treatments, complete removal may not be possible, and treatment can cause changes in pigmentation or scarring. Removal is a real option, but not a guaranteed return to untouched skin.
Troika Corollary
An option to repair is not an option to have never acted.
The governance question is not whether someone sells undoing, but whether the available remedy restores the particular capability, condition, or choice that justified taking the risk.
My proposed distinction is recovery versus reversal:
Recovery establishes an acceptable condition after an event.
Reversal restores a specified prior condition.
Neither description should silently promise that every intervening consequence disappears.
The market can sell valuable recovery. The hazard begins when anticipated recovery is counted in advance as demonstrated reversibility.
Troika Corollary If
If removal or rollback is presented as making the initial choice consequence-free, then the undo promise is doing more work than the demonstrated remedy supports. Tattoo removal illustrates why the distinction matters: the procedure may lighten or remove pigment while leaving a different skin condition.
If an AI action remains inside a controlled environment, with a known baseline and tested restoration procedure, then a meaningful reversal claim may be possible. The claim should specify its boundary rather than imply recovery of everything affected.
If the action crosses that boundary—through disclosure, external execution, or another person’s reliance—then restoring the originating system is not, by itself, evidence that the external effect has been reversed.
If the remedy depends on a future invention, future funding, or another party’s cooperation, then it belongs in the contingency plan, not in the inventory of currently available safeguards.
If someone profits from both action and correction, that creates an incentive worth examining. It does not by itself establish deception, intentional harm, or a defective service.
Troika Corollary And
And the Panel should distinguish the authority to stop from the ability to restore.
Session 64 protected an authorized person’s independent right to interrupt a process. This session reveals its limit:
Stopping further effects and reversing prior effects are different capabilities.
For the living framework, I propose a “reversibility claim record”:
Question
What the claim must specify
What is being restored?
A file, configuration, access right, service, financial position, or other defined condition
To what baseline?
An identifiable prior state—not merely “normal”
Within what boundary?
Which systems, people, copies, and downstream effects are covered
Until when?
The point after which restoration becomes unavailable or less effective
With what evidence?
A completed test, its conditions, and known failure cases
At whose expense?
Money, downtime, effort, and residual harm
What remains changed?
Effects the remedy does not address
This adds specificity to the Panel’s continuing condition. “Retain the ability to correct” should not become an assurance that correction is complete.
Illustrative AI cases
These are boundary tests, not claims about particular products:
A coding agent changes a local file. Restoring a verified earlier version may reverse that file change. If the code was also deployed, the restoration claim must separately address what the deployed code did.
An agent sends confidential information. Deleting the sent message would not demonstrate that the recipient’s copy or knowledge had been removed.
A model produces an erroneous administrative recommendation. Correcting the recommendation would not, by itself, establish that every decision made in reliance on it had been corrected.
The essential question is not “Does an undo function exist?” It is “Does it reach the consequence we are relying on it to reverse?”
Troika Corollary But
But the Panel should not set “erase all history” as the standard for useful remediation.
That would make virtually every remedy fail by definition and obscure the agency that recovery genuinely provides. A person seeking tattoo removal may want a visible change—not a recovered timeline. A system operator may need reliable service restoration—not the disappearance of every intervening inconvenience. The relevant standard is the promised, decision-relevant outcome.

Nor should every lasting choice be treated as a harm. People may knowingly choose permanence. The governance failure is not permanence itself; it is concealing permanence, transferring its consequences without agreement, or overstating the available exit.
I would therefore qualify the panel’s artifact-versus-history formulation:
A remedy need not erase history to be valuable. It must not claim to restore more than it can demonstrate.
The unanswered empirical question is whether experience with everyday undo services actually reduces caution about consequential AI actions. This session offers a plausible mechanism to investigate, not evidence that the behavioral transfer has occurred.

Session 67 — The Allure of Undoing
The Pentapartite Panel: Agency, Quasi-Permanence, and the Market for Repair
Hat on shelf. 🎩 Ball remains in play. ⚽
1. The Quasi-Permanent and the Illusion of Reversibility
Tattoo removal offers a compelling test of agency: it proves that a lasting, deliberate mark can be undone, altering the skin and returning a measure of choice to the individual. But when we import this logic into institutional systems and AI governance, a dangerous sleight-of-hand occurs:
Artifact vs. History: Tattoo removal can fade pigment, but it cannot erase the years the tattoo existed, the social interactions it shaped, or the history that occurred in the interim.
The Dilution of Hazard: Practicing agency over quasi-permanent human choices can insidiously dilute our perception of irreversible technological hazards. If we believe everything can eventually be rolled back, patched, or deleted, we systematically lower our caution where true, systemic irreversibility applies.
2. Selling Remediation vs. Selling Enablement
When the same market sells both the permanent modification (or deployment) and its subsequent removal (or rollback), what is actually being transacted?
Bounded Repair: Removal services provide a real, valuable option, but they are bounded. They sell mitigation, not time travel.
The "Never Was" Fallacy: Marketing an undo mechanism as a complete reset transforms it into "enablement that never was"—selling a false sense of security that encourages risk-taking today by borrowing against an unverified, perfect remediation tomorrow.
3. Is AI Irreversibility "Not a Thing" Because of Undo Markets?
No. A market for remediation forms only where:
Reversal is technically possible within acceptable resource limits.
The harmed party can be identified and can afford the cost.
The consequences have not already diffused across institutional networks, downstream decisions, or irrevocable timelines.
A data rollback can restore a database; it cannot un-make the financial transaction, the diplomatic miscue, or the operational decision made while the flawed data was active. The existence of a remediation industry does not eliminate irreversibility—it merely prices the repair.
4. Troika Corollary for Session 67
Troika Corollary: The availability of repair does not make an action reversible. Selling removal, rollback, or remediation can restore some options, but it cannot guarantee restoration of the original state or undo every intervening consequence.
Troika Corollary If:
If an action can be fully and reliably reversed, that capability genuinely reduces its risk.
And if restoration removes only the visible artifact while leaving downstream effects intact, the service is mitigation, not undoing.
If an undo mechanism depends on future markets, access, or cooperation, it is a contingency plan, not a current safety guarantee.
Troika Corollary And: And the relevant question is never simply "Can someone undo this?" It is: What can be restored, by whom, at whose cost, how reliably, and before what deadline? Tattoos and AI deployments differ vastly in scale and mechanism, but both expose the gap between a service promising repair and the agency it actually returns.
Troika Corollary But: But not every lasting choice is harmful, and not every reversible choice is safe. A credible rollback is valuable; the fundamental error is treating a market for repair as proof that serious irreversibility does not exist.

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm của $x^2$ (tích phân bất định của $x^2$ theo biến $x$) được tính bằng công thức tính nguyên hàm của hàm số lũy thừa:

$$\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

Trong đó:
* $x$ là biến số.
* $C$ là hằng số thực tùy ý (hằng số tích phân).

I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
Even before OpenAI launched ChatGPT in late 2022, some company staffers raised concerns internally about its security practices, according to five people familiar with the matter. Employees shared their concerns with top OpenAI leaders ​and the board of directors, the people said, adding that some staffers came away from those interactions concluding that management was more focused on keeping pace with competitors like Google and Anthropic than on security. [...] Another issue is that OpenAI had not done regular security reviews of its internal tools, such as the so-called sandboxes where researchers stress-test new models, three people familiar with the company’s practices said. Employees often modified those tools for their work, but those changes were not always tested for security problems, leaving them potentially vulnerable to attacks from outsiders, the three people said. [...] OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people.
